item.research_question: What are the bulk critical resolved shear stress (CRSS), the size effect scaling exponent, the stacking fault energy, and the magnitude of solid-solution strengthening in the equatomic CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy?
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of high-purity elements in argon, cold-rolling (60% reduction), recrystallization at 1,173–1,473 K; single-crystal micropillars (1.0–8.3 μm edge length) machined via FIB at 30 kV; bulk polycrystals with grain sizes of 8, 70, and 340 μm
item.test_conditions: Micropillar compression at room temperature (strain rate 1 × 10⁻¹ s⁻¹); bulk polycrystal compression at room temperature and 77 K (strain rate 1 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹); TEM analysis at 200 kV
key_findings: Bulk room temperature CRSS is estimated at 33–43 MPa, approximately 10 times higher than that of pure nickel (~3.2 MPa).
CRSS follows an inverse power-law scaling with pillar size with an exponent of –0.63, independent of crystal orientation.
Stacking fault energy is determined to be 30 ± 5 mJ/m² based on Shockley partial separations of 3.5–4.5 nm (screw) and 5–8 nm (edge).
Yield stress at 77 K (260 MPa for 340 μm grain size) is slightly more than twice the yield stress at room temperature (127 MPa).
Dislocations are planar and smoothly curved with no preferred line orientation, indicating no significant anisotropy in edge and screw mobilities.
The shear-modulus-normalized CRSS of the HEA corresponds to a hypothetical binary alloy with 20–50 at.% solute concentration and ~4% atomic size misfit.
Young's and shear moduli are ~10% smaller than pure Ni, while the bulk modulus is 24% smaller than pure Ni.
item.mechanism: The high CRSS is attributed to thermal solid-solution hardening driven by atomic size misfit (~4% between Cr and Co/Fe) rather than severe lattice distortion alone; the low stacking fault energy combined with a high shear modulus leads to wide partial separations that inhibit cross-slip, while the absence of orientation dependence suggests similar mobilities for edge and screw segments.
item.limitations: The study notes that Goldschmidt radii may not provide accurate size misfit values, requiring ab initio calculations to estimate the true misfit of ~4.1%; the solid-solution hardening estimate is described as a rough order-of-magnitude calculation.
item.future_work: The authors state that full results of deformation experiments on bulk single crystals of the HEA will be published elsewhere and that additional studies are needed to improve understanding of factors like impurity contamination affecting CRSS.
quotes: CRSS depends on pillar size with an inverse power-law scaling exponent of –0.63 independent of orientation.
yielding and subsequent flow occurs smoothly without any discontinuities such as yield drops or serrated flow.
The stacking fault energy of the HEA deduced from the separation distance of the two, coupled, Shockley partial dislocations is 30 ± 5 mJ/m2.
